text:
mara: Proposal: change admission control for gpu-pool 'large'. Instead of hard reject when queue depth > 250, admit a bounded "slowpath" that processes best-effort requests at reduced priority and returns Retry-After hints to clients. This should smooth 5xx spikes and avoid thundering rejects during short bursts. Thoughts?

kevin: Curious about cost impact — admitting more requests even on slowpath still uses GPU cycles. What's the expected p99 tail tradeoff vs extra tokens?

mara: Good call. Expecting higher overall token cost but lower 5xx rate and lower user-perceived error rate. We can cap slowpath concurrency and run a canary to measure cost delta.

devin: How do we pick which requests go to slowpath? Per-customer tier + request hints? Suggest header x-ri-priority or a per-token cost budget on accounts.

sophia: Also need clear signal to trigger *drop* if slowpath backs up: admit slowpath until backlog > 6m processing time, then reject. Otherwise we'll keep delaying into infinite queue.

mara: Agree. Proposed config (rough):
```
admission:
  policy: priority_slowpath
  queue_threshold: 250
  slowpath:
    concurrency_limit: 200
    rate_multiplier: 0.3  # each slowpath request gets 30% of normal token throughput
    max_buffer_ms: 360000
  hard_reject_trigger_ms: 360000
```
